Subject: Performance SLOs & Load Test Plan (next steps)

Hi Taylor / Sanjay —

Thanks again for the demo this morning. Quick recap of the SLOs you called out and the plan I heard:

- P95 latency target: <= 200ms for the /v1/generate endpoint (streaming enabled; partial tokens acceptable)
- Sustained throughput: 50 req/s for the customer-facing service (peak bursts up to ~100 req/s for short spikes)
- Concurrent connections: ~40 concurrent streams/clients
- Streaming: required for user-facing flows (we'll validate chunked SSE behavior)

Next steps / ask from our side:
1) Customer-led load test window: proposed Aug 4, 09:00–12:00 PST. Please confirm or suggest an alternative.
2) Provide a test account (username/email + org) we can provision a dedicated API key for (we will issue a scoped test key that can be revoked).
3) IP allowlist: we'll need any FinCo network IPs or proxy egress ranges to allowlist on our side if you plan to hit from corporate network; likewise, please allowlist our egress ranges so your test harness can reach the test endpoint (we'll provide those).
4) Test artifacts: attaching a draft k6 script and a reference Locust file. Feel free to reuse or swap in your existing k6/Locust scripts.

Attachments: draft-k6-script.js (stub), locustfile.py (stub)

Technical notes for the test:
- We'll provision a test API key scoped to the /v1/generate route and streaming. Token will be rate-limited to ensure isolation.
- Recommended load profile: 10m ramp to 50 rps, sustain for 60–120m, 3x short spikes to 100 rps to exercise autoscaling/fallbacks.
- We'll surface per-request latency (p50/p95/p99), model-side GPU utilization, and request queue metrics during the test.

Let me know if Aug 4 works and who on your side will own the test (name + email). Once we confirm, I'll create the test key and send the allowlist details.

Thanks,
Marissa

Subject: Re: Performance SLOs & Load Test Plan (next steps) — technical notes\n
Looping in a few technical specifics from the serving/runtime side so expectations are aligned:

- Connection & concurrency: our serving tier accepts long-lived streaming connections. By default we cap to ~2000 total concurrent streams per cluster; per-API-key connection limits are configurable — for this test we'll set a per-key soft cap of 200 concurrent connections to avoid noisy-neighbor effects.
- Queuing and burst behavior: short spikes up to 3x sustained RPS should enqueue briefly; we'll monitor request queue length and backpressure signals. If you see queueing beyond ~250ms average, flag us and we can scale a warm-up pool.
- GPU utilization metrics: we'll stream GPU metrics (util %, memory) and model latency buckets; please include these in your post-test analysis.
- Recommended concrete load profile:
  * 10m ramp to 60 rps (to test autoscaler)
  * 60m sustain at 50 rps
  * 3x 5m spikes to 100 rps with at least 10m between spikes
  * Run a short embedding-only job (10m at 10 rps) to validate mixed traffic handling.

I'll attach load_test_steps.md with step-by-step commands for Locust and k6 (including how to enable streaming in the k6 websocket/SSE plugin). Please run the first smoke run at low scale and paste logs if anything looks off.

-Aditya
